audit_findings.title: Finance-lease asset costs may disappear from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $10.079 million of 2025 finance-lease principal payments, equal to 68.1% of the $14.8 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: OE may add back $10.565 million of finance-lease ROU amortization without deducting the corresponding asset-acquisition cash requirement
audit_findings.evidence: In 2025, the principal financing outflows were related to dividend payments of $61.1 million, payments related to finance leases of $10.1 million, and distributions to noncontrolling interests of $5.7 million which were primarily to distribute proceeds from the 2025 refranchising transaction to our noncontrolling interest.
audit_findings.explanation: The cash payment and related amortization are demonstrated, but the supplied record does not establish whether the OE calculation captured either finance-lease principal or asset additions. If omitted while ROU amortization was added back, the error is large relative to the anchor and would materially reduce every scenario.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile 2025 D&A add-backs to finance-lease ROU amortization and maintenance investment; rerun OE deducting maintenance finance-lease additions or principal exactly once.

audit_findings.title: FY2025 is not a clean post-refranchising perimeter
audit_findings.magnitude: $17.053 million 2025 pre-tax gain and 85 refranchised restaurants; recurring post-sale OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The transaction affects anchor OE through the disposal gain, restaurant earnings, royalties, commissary margins, capital expenditures and NCI allocations
audit_findings.evidence: On November 24, 2025, the Company completed the refranchising of 85 Domestic Company-owned restaurants previously owned and operated by Colonel’s Limited, LLC, a consolidated joint venture, to Pie Investments, an existing third-party franchisee (“Buyer”), for total proceeds of $35.7 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The sale occurred on November 24, so FY2025 contains nearly a full year of the former company-owned operations but little of the recurring franchise model. The $17.053 million gain alone exceeds the $14.8 million anchor, although the record does not show whether it was removed. Future royalties and reduced capital needs could offset lost store earnings, so the recurring direction remains mixed.
audit_findings.action: Confirm removal of the disposal gain and prepare a post-sale pro forma replacing the 85 stores' revenue, expenses, capital needs and NCI cash flows with recurring royalties and commissary economics; rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The latest debt burden is paired with stale interest expense
audit_findings.magnitude: Comparable debt plus finance-lease liabilities increased $8.267 million, or 1.1%, from $763.060 million at year-end 2025 to $771.327 million at June 2026; annualized H1 2026 net interest expense was $38.398 million versus $40.769 million in 2025
audit_findings.mechanism: Because this is an equity-level OE model, financing affects value through after-tax recurring interest in OE rather than a second deduction of debt principal
audit_findings.evidence: Our outstanding debt as of December 28, 2025 was $722.3 million, which was comprised of $400.0 million outstanding under the Notes, $200.0 million outstanding under the Term Loan, and $122.3 million outstanding under the PJI Revolving Facility.
audit_findings.explanation: The asserted approximately $49 million increase compares June debt including $37.812 million of finance-lease liabilities with year-end debt excluding $40.803 million of finance-lease liabilities. On a comparable basis, the increase was only 1.1%, while filed H1 interest expense actually ran below 2025. Thus no material interest understatement is demonstrated, and the available scale is not capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Recalculate normalized after-tax interest using June corporate debt, the fixed-note coupon, floating-rate margins and swaps; separately identify PJMF debt and finance-lease interest, without deducting principal again.

audit_findings.title: Parent earnings may be mixed with consolidated cash-flow components
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.586 million of 2025 NCI income, equal to 10.7% of the $14.8 million anchor; total ownership-basis distortion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: OE may start with parent-attributable income while adding and subtracting consolidated D&A, working capital, capital expenditures and lease cash flows; shares represent only common-parent claims
audit_findings.evidence: Net income included income attributable to noncontrolling interests of $1.6 million during 2025 and $0.7 million for the prior year.
audit_findings.explanation: The parent-versus-consolidated ownership bases are demonstrably different, and the NCI income benchmark is meaningful relative to the anchor. However, approximately $1.0 million of that NCI income related to the disposal gain, and the record does not provide the NCI shares of each OE adjustment. The existence and materiality of a net recurring error therefore remain unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile every 2025 OE component to the parent's economic ownership, including the Colonel's joint venture through November 24, remove NCI portions from consolidated cash-flow adjustments, and rerun the anchor.

audit_findings.title: Consolidated cash may not all be distributable to common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: At least $3.751 million, equal to $0.110 per diluted share and 1.67% of the $225 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds consolidated cash even though PJMF cash is legally dedicated to advertising and is not excess cash distributable to common shareholders
audit_findings.evidence: The assets and liabilities of PJMF, which are utilized solely for the Company’s advertising and promotional programs, were as follows in the Consolidated Balance Sheets:
audit_findings.explanation: The June filing demonstrates that $3.751 million of the $28.490 million bridge balance belonged to PJMF and was solely for advertising programs. Excluding that amount reduces value by only about $0.11 per share. Even excluding the entire $28.490 million would reduce value by approximately $0.84 per share, insufficient to change the conclusion against the $22.68 market price.
audit_findings.action: Trace June cash by legal entity and restriction, exclude PJMF cash, restricted or escrowed balances and required operating cash, and update the bridge without changing OE.
